newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BATSMEN DEFY SRI LANKA BOWLING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN BATSMEN DEFY SRI LANKA BOWLING.

text.p: Pakistan's batsmen continued to defy the Sri Lanka bowling, adding a quick 90 runs for the loss of only one wicket in the morning session on the third day of the second and final test on Monday.
At lunch, Pakistan were 236 for five wickets in reply to Sri Lanka's first innings total of 331.
Left-hander Asif Mujtaba played a key role in Sri Lanka's failure to make early inroads in Pakistan batting. He played patiently to remain undefeated on 49 at the interval.
Mujtaba received a repreive at 44 when Sanath Jayasuriya dropped a sitter at second slip off left-arm pace bowler Sajeeva de Silva when the second new ball was only three overs old.
Mujtaba has so far blunted Sri Lanka's bowling attack for 260 minutes hitting seven fours.
His partner Moin Khan was the more enterprising in a stand of 89 for the sixth wicket.
Moin's contribution in the stand was an unbeaten 66 scored off 85 balls, which included one six and six fours.
When he made 43, Moin passed 1,000 tuns in test cricket playing in his 26th test for Pakistan.
Soon afterwards he completed his sixth test 50 off 78 balls with the aid of one six and five fours.
Sri Lanka had an early breakthrough when Pakistan's overnight batsman Inzamam-ul-Haq edged the first ball of the day off Chaminda Vaas to wicket keeper Romesh Kaluwitharana.
Inzamam, usually known for his flamboyant batting, scored a sedate 43 in 165 minutes with just three fours.
Scores: Sri Lanka 331, Pakistan 236 for five wickets at lunch.
